headline: CPI 8:30, hike odds 85%, Waller floats 50bp, Brent $90.48, Kospi +4.4%, $42bn 10y auction 1pm
stance: The oil premium is unwinding faster than the Fed premium: Brent under $90, December hike odds 85%+. CPI at 8:30 and $42bn of 10y at 1pm decide if Monday's rebound holds.

news.head: SoftBank first net loss in two years; +13.9% Tokyo
news.body: ¥768bn H1 loss: ¥597bn write-down on US data-center power equipment, derivative loss on Intel shares. Arm Q3 revenue guide $1.54bn, above consensus.

news.head: Infineon +3% at the open, +6% later, on 2027 guide
news.body: Revenue growth above 20% in 2027, profitability up about 5 points, on data-center, power and auto demand. Shares +3.1% (~3am ET), +6.1% by 4:15am ET.

news.head: Nvidia -4.2% Monday, lowest close since Apr 7
news.body: Board probe of Huang continues; a former SEC chair questioned his disclosures Monday. Shares +1.0% after hours Monday. Chips rallied without their leader.

news.head: Anthropic may start IPO marketing today
news.body: Roadshow could begin as early as Tuesday despite last week's vol spike. First large AI listing since the midterm selloff; the book is the next test.

implications: Oil and the Fed have decoupled: Brent -24% from its October peak, December hike odds 85%+. CPI at 8:30 decides whether 50bp enters the December conversation.
Two-step day for duration. Core 0.3%+ at 8:30 meets Waller's 50bp line; $42bn of 10y goes to auction at 1pm into it.

watch.head: CPI 8:30: core 0.2% consensus, no y/y published
watch.body: Headline 0.3% expected, from 0.6%. Core 0.3%+ meets Waller's 50bp threshold; 0.1% or lower reopens the pause case. Monthly figures only, shutdown gap.

watch.head: 10y auction 1pm, $42bn
watch.body: Follows Monday's 3y: bid-to-cover 2.53 vs 2.62 prior, record direct share. $25bn 30y Thursday. Watch indirect take, not the yield.

watch.head: Fed speakers: Logan 10:50, Schmid 1:30, Bowman 3:30
watch.body: All after CPI. Barkin overnight: wait for the data before December. Waller already on record for 25bp minimum, 50bp on a hot core.

watch.head: CoreWeave reports after today's close
watch.body: First neocloud results since the midterms. Backlog and financing terms matter more than the quarter. Nebius follows Thursday.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Brent $90.48, -2.3% (~4:30am ET), under $90 intraday for the first time since August. Iran's proposal via Qatar is with the White House.
December hike odds 85% overnight, 96% after Waller (~4am ET). Waller in London: 25bp in December even on soft CPI, 50bp if core prints 0.3% or more.
OPEC October output +1.38mb/d, 90% of pre-war February. Saudi East-West pipeline hit Monday, fire out. Rubio: Iranian demands unacceptable.
sections.positioning: No new COT extreme this week. Euro specs 1st %ile for 7 weeks; 5y Treasury longs 94th for 9 weeks. Background, not a trigger.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Monday was the S&P's best day since April 8; SOX +6.85%, every sector up. Futures: S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq 100 -0.15%, Dow +0.5% (~3:50am ET).
Nikkei +2.87% at Tuesday's close. Kospi +4.39%, buy-side sidecar at the open; Taiex +2.5%. Stoxx 600 +0.9% (~3am ET), within 1% of its August record.
Russell 2000 +3.15% Monday, ahead of the Nasdaq. The S&P is back to its pre-election level after a 4.4% post-midterm drop.
sections.positioning: COT unchanged: Nasdaq 100 longs 89th %ile, Russell 2000 99th, VIX shorts 10th. Monday's rally ran into full long books, not empty ones.

single_name.note: New to the screen Nov 9, score 5. Insider buy filed Oct 29, above its 200-day line, 3.3 days to cover. Regional bank, outside the AI chain.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Chip-maker 5y CDS near 160bp, from about 80bp in August. First time above the hyperscaler basket in three months.
Neoclouds are borrowing from banks, not bonds: a HY deal shelved in October became a $3.5bn secured bank facility.
Listed BDCs 0.89x NAV at Monday's close, an 11% discount. Spread marks run to Friday; Monday's rally is not in them yet.
sections.positioning: Dealer IG inventory mid-range, 44th %ile of 3 years. No credit COT extreme.
